answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain custody of 1,000 unique data shards to verify active storage capacity. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct files across the network. A verifier requests unpredictable segments like the zenith of the sun, ensuring every shard is hollow of duplication. This shard acts as a relic of proof, checked at the dawn of every epoch. Any failure to return segments triggers a permanent slash, ensuring the cost of faking identities remains strictly proportional.
